notes: Historical financials are from Nucor’s 2025 Form 10-K (covering 2023–2025): revenue = Net sales; EBIT is constructed as (Earnings before income taxes and noncontrolling interests) + (interest expense (income), net) using the sign convention shown in the statement. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

D&A is constructed as (Depreciation + Amortization) from the consolidated statements of cash flows; capex is taken as (Capital expenditures) from the consolidated cash flow statement (absolute values). ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

NWC is calculated at each fiscal year-end using a working-capital approximation from balance sheet line items: (Accounts receivable + Inventories + Other current assets) - (Accounts payable + Salaries/wages accruals + Accrued expenses/other current liabilities), excluding cash/short-term investments and excluding short-term debt/current portion of long-term debt. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

2026 capex assumption is anchored to Nucor’s stated estimate that capital expenditures for 2026 are approximately $2.50 billion; the model converts this into capex_pct_sales. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))
Base-case forecast drivers (growth, margins, DA%, capex%, NWC%) are modeled assumptions intended for DCF QA chaining; they are not company-issued multi-year guidance.

Comps multiples: EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA are taken from StockAnalysis valuation ratios and treated as NTM proxies due to data-label limitations in the fetched pages; where forward PE or EV/EBITDA was n/a, the fields are set to null. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/stld/statistics/))

NOLs: nol_balance uses state + foreign NOL carryforwards disclosed in the 10-K; nol_utilization_pct was not disclosed in a usable form, so it is set to null. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Assumptions: WACC, terminal growth, terminal exit EBITDA multiple, and terminal method are DCF-model inputs and not directly disclosed by the company; they are sober base-case choices for valuation sensitivity.

catalysts: Sustained improvement (or deterioration) in realized steel pricing and product spreads as demand/backlogs evolve through 2026.
Capacity expansion execution and utilization ramps (and any associated impairment risk) as new/expanded facilities contribute to earnings power.
Industry and policy dynamics (import pressure, trade policy, and domestic construction activity) that can shift margins faster than volumes.
company_overview: Nucor manufactures steel and steel products and also produces/procures ferrous and non-ferrous materials used in its steel manufacturing business. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Operates three segments: steel mills, steel products, and raw materials; most operations and customers are located in North America. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Uses scrap steel as its primary raw material in electric arc furnace (“EAF”) steelmaking; in 2025 recycled ~20 million gross tons of scrap steel. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))
current_context: Q4 2025: net sales of $7.69 billion and net earnings attributable to Nucor stockholders of $378 million (diluted EPS $1.64). ([investors.nucor.com](https://investors.nucor.com/news/news-details/2026/Nucor-Reports-Results-for-the-Fourth-Quarter-of-2025/default.aspx))

Full-year 2025: net sales of $32.49 billion and net earnings attributable to Nucor stockholders of $1.74 billion (diluted EPS $7.52). ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Balance sheet strength: cash and cash equivalents plus short-term investments of $2.70 billion at end of Q4 2025. ([investors.nucor.com](https://investors.nucor.com/news/news-details/2026/Nucor-Reports-Results-for-the-Fourth-Quarter-of-2025/default.aspx))

2026 outlook framing: management highlighted robust end-market demand and expects higher earnings beginning in early 2026. ([investors.nucor.com](https://investors.nucor.com/news/news-details/2026/Nucor-Reports-Results-for-the-Fourth-Quarter-of-2025/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue trajectory assumes modest steel-cycle growth from 2025 levels, with gradual normalization rather than mean-reversion to extreme peaks. (Base-case assumption; not company-guaranteed.)

Base-case EBIT margin rises toward a mid-cycle target as utilization and realized pricing stabilize; this is consistent with Nucor’s historically cyclical earnings power. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Capital intensity steps down versus 2025: 2026 capex is guided/estimated at approximately $2.50 billion, informing capex as a % of sales in the model. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Working-capital intensity is kept roughly stable (NWC as a % of sales), reflecting an industrial cash conversion that varies less than pricing/volume over short horizons. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))
key_risks: Steel price and cost volatility (scrap, natural gas/electricity, and iron ore) compressing margins versus the base-case path. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))

Downcycle demand leading to lower utilization and weaker operating leverage than assumed. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/a1091887-5d3b-4cc2-b1c5-7623695cc1b5.pdf))
Execution/asset risks, including potential impairments or delays that affect the margin and capex trajectory assumed in the DCF.

valuation_summary: DCF base case uses EBIT margins that interpolate between 2024/2025 performance and a normalized target, with a terminal growth rate consistent with long-run macro assumptions. (Base-case assumption.)
Terminal value anchors on an economically sensible exit EBITDA multiple consistent with large-cap steel peers, applied under an average terminal method. (Assumption.)

Peer comps provide a directional check on EV/earnings and forward P/E levels; where NTM inputs are unavailable, the closest available valuation ratio proxy is used. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/stld/statistics/))
